failure_summary: render_decision.zones.aliases 'you-key-line' (windows:c2r1,c3r1,c4r1,c5r1, role 'the whole four-in-a-row line you are playing for') and 'you-key-square' (c3r1, role 'a single square completing you's four-in-a-row line') are board-FALSE on their truthBoard 'decision': visualize_board.sh 334 shows c4r1 and c5r1 are GREEN (opponent, player 1) discs while the blunderer is player 2, so that bottom-row window can never be the player's line - both runs echoed the false ownership verbatim and failed A4; secondarily link.text says the opponent 'occupies c2r1, completing their double threat' while render_decision.finalMovestring 33432 has the opponent occupying c3r1 with c2r1 still empty (a threat square), which run 0 echoed, and run 0 emitted an unoffered [term:double_threat] slug (zones.terms is empty) failing G7b (prompt_confusion, production-fidelity run - gpt-5.4-mini, so model capability cannot be separated from prompt defect).
notes: n_runs is 2 for this run (not 5); A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 sub-sampling therefore covered every run. A4 run0: 'preserved the four-in-a-row line from column 2 to column 5 for you' - false, that window holds two opponent discs (c4r1, c5r1 = X on board 334). A4 run1: same ownership claim ('keep your four-in-a-row line on column 2, row 1-column 5, row 1') PLUS 'you left column 2, row 1 open, so your opponent could claim the shared spot' - the shared cell is c3r1 (opponentPunishment.tie.sharedCells=['c3r1'], and 33432 plays c3r1), not c2r1. A7b run1: 'the shared spot' is anchored to the just-named c2r1, which is not the shared cell, so the referent resolves to the wrong object. G5 both runs: the offered alias roles above are the false rendered entries (render bug to report, not narrate around). G7 run0: raw carries [term:double_threat] but render_decision.zones.terms is empty (mechanical G7b_offered=fail); the guard stripped it, so servedExplanation is clean and A5 is unaffected. A5 passes both runs incl. A5b (player 2 + opening): neither run says the player is lost and both give a hold-the-line frame ('the tougher defense was column 3' / 'you should have played column 3 to take away...'). A3 passes: the named tactic (opponent's bottom-row open three at c3r1-c4r1-c5r1 giving double major threats at c2r1 and c6r1 on 33432) is real and decisive; solver on 334 scores the better column 3 (0-idx 2) at +2 and the played column 4 (0-idx 3) at -18. A7c passes both: the fork-creating square c3r1 is named in both runs (no *-fork-pivot handle was offered; it coincides with the required you-key-square).
